experimental_method: Specific gravity of dilute gas-saturated solutions relative to air-free conductivity water by a communicating-tube (Frivold) method in a thermostatted copper block (dye-flow null detection, volume withdrawn read in a capillary burette); concentration from the measured gas partial pressure via Henry's law and the solubilities of Claussen and Polglase; apparent molal volume from Eq. (1).
uncertainties_stated: Specific gravity to one part in 10^7 (blank runs never exceeded this); air-bath temperature +/-0.01 C, columns equal within +/-0.00001 C. Henry's law assumed valid within 0.5 %. Author: precision for the aliphatic hydrocarbons considerably less than for benzene because the concentration data are less accurate. Gases 99 mol% pure (research grade).
quality_remarks: Apparent molal volume taken equal to the partial molal volume (author: found identical in these very dilute solutions). Concentrations y are not analysed but calculated from literature solubility (Claussen and Polglase 1952). Two methane values (36.2 at 16.8 C, 35.9 at 35.1 C) flagged by the author with footnote a and omitted from the averages. Recomputed average of the 35.1 C methane block without the flagged value is 38.13, printed 38.2; other averages reproduce. Temperatures 16.8-35.1 C only; pressure not stated (near atmospheric).
